wordpress: Release blocker — plugin/includes/class-availability.php:43: A reservation whose expires_at equals the supplied UTC clock is excluded from the REST count, even though the contract says it still occupies a place. The dashboard includes it, so a REST client can show the place as available while the dashboard counts it as occupied. Restore the inclusive comparison and add an equality regression case for both consumers. The retrospective history comparison has a different documented contract and is not a finding. The supplied unit tests pass for one second before and after expiry, but do not establish behavior at equality. No WordPress integration, package, deployment, or live-site evidence is supplied; the patch has not been released, and go-live is blocked until the defect is corrected and appropriately verified.
service:
Release blocker — service/routes/exports.js:20: The change removes the server-side workspace membership check. An authenticated user who obtains an export ID belonging to another workspace can receive its private project names; an opaque ID and a user ID do not establish permission. Restore authorization against the export's owning workspace and test a different-workspace user, including the approved integration's authorized access.

Follow-up — service/jobs/digest.js:36: Settings are loaded once per row even though they are identical throughout a digest build. A 500-row digest makes 500 settings queries instead of one, adding avoidable database work to the scheduled job. Load settings once per build and cover query count; the packet contains no timing or load evidence to establish the operational impact or make this a separate release blocker.

The supplied tests establish the covered member success and three-row formatting cases only; they do not establish cross-workspace denial or query efficiency. No integration environment, runtime load, release, or live-service evidence is supplied. Go-live is blocked by the authorization defect until it is fixed and verified.
